Two minor quote-timestamp errors need fixing: (1) script_coverage tax_credit_qualifier customer_quote 'Yes. Yeah. Yes.' is mistimed at 02:22 (that's where the rep begins the qualifier ask) — correct ts is ~02:45, right after the rep's '670' self-correction. (2) script_coverage button_up customer_quote 'Alright. Sure. Thank you.' is mistimed at 03:59 (rep is speaking then) — correct ts is 04:31, the actual end-of-call line.

More substantively: the entire analysis leans too heavily on one ambiguous customer line at 03:26 ('We should next week in the afternoon') to build its top coaching priority, its outcome-dispute/fragile-booking framing, and its handoff brief's central risk flag. This line should be reconciled against the customer's very next statement at 03:44-03:47 ('I should be good with any of the time'), which directly softens or contradicts a firm next-week-only preference. Revise the trajectory_verdict, coaching_focus priority 1, multi_touch_patterns, and handoff_brief to either (a) present this as a genuine but unresolved ambiguity rather than a confirmed steamrolled objection, or (b) explicitly weigh both customer statements and explain why the 03:26 line should still dominate despite the contradiction.

Also fix schema_reference in cherry_pick_moments[0]: this call is an inbound callback (customer returning a call, no Tesla framing anywhere in transcript), so citing intros.tesla is inaccurate — should reference intros.standard or note that neither scripted intro variant fits an inbound callback.

Two missed moments worth adding: (1) the customer's origin story at 00:27 ('I think I've made a call from someone called Kenny... trying to call back') is the actual legitimacy anchor in this call and should inform the intro_legitimacy assessment. (2) the customer's 'Can I verify?' at 01:44 is a distinct, concrete missed opportunity — the customer offers to confirm the bill figure and the rep never follows up, which is more specific evidence for the bill_document_audit gap than what's currently cited. Consider also elevating the rep's unchecked assumption on title ownership (02:24, 'which I assume is no issue for you') given the schema flags title_co_owners as a required/critical Verify item.
